<explanation>
Based on our analysis of Meridian’s file structure and README, here’s how you can create an accurate and detailed system design diagram for the project.

1. Project Context & Purpose
   - Meridian is a marketing mix modeling (MMM) framework. It is designed to help advertisers run Bayesian causal inference-based MMM analyses. The system handles large-scale geo-level (and national-level) data, provides MCMC sampling (with GPU-supported No U Turn Sampler), and outputs analytical summaries and visualizations to aid budget planning and marketing optimization.
   - Your diagram should reflect that this is essentially a specialized modeling and analytics framework with clear separations between data ingestion, analysis, model building, and result visualization components.

2. Identify and Outline Main Components
   Based on the file tree and README, you can identify the following major components:

   a. Data Layer:
      - Components: Located in the “meridian/data” directory.
      - Responsibilities: Handling data input, sample data management, simulated data, time coordinates, and argument building. This part of the system is responsible for loading, preprocessing, and coordinating data extraction.
      - Diagram: Represent this as a “Data Ingestion & Preprocessing” module with subcomponents (Input Data, Load Utilities, Time Coordination, etc.), with arrows feeding data into the analysis and modeling layers.

   b. Analysis Module:
      - Components: Found under “meridian/analysis”.
      - Responsibilities: Implementing various analytics functions including summarization, optimization, formatting, visualization, and reporting. It also includes Jinja2 templates for generating reports and dashboards (HTML-based templates for cards, charts, tables, etc.).
      - Diagram: Draw this as a distinct “Analysis & Visualization” component. Show that it consumes processed data, produces insights, and formats outputs via templates.

   c. Modeling Module:
      - Components: Located in “meridian/model”.
      - Responsibilities: Handling the core MMM methodologies. This includes building the marketing mix model, setting model specifications, performing MCMC sampling using NUTS, managing priors/posteriors, and implementing transformations (e.g., adstock, media functions).
      - Diagram: Represent this as the “MMM Modeling and Inference Engine” with submodules for (i) Bayesian sampling (posterior and prior samplers), (ii) transformation and optimization utilities, and (iii) statistical model components. Connect it with the data layer (ingesting preprocessed inputs) and analysis layer (supplying outputs for visualizations).

   d. External and Supporting Components:
      - GitHub Actions/CI Integration: The “.github” directory includes workflows for CI/CD, build, version checks, and custom actions. Indicate in the diagram an “Automated Testing & Deployment” component that ensures quality and version integrity.
      - Demo Notebooks: The “demo” directory provides Jupyter notebooks (e.g., Getting Started and RF Demo) that allow users to interact with the library. Even though they are not part of the core runtime architecture, you might include a “User Demo / Notebook” box that shows how external users interact with the framework.
      - Build and Distribution: Files like “setup.py”, “pyproject.toml”, and “MANIFEST.in” indicate standard Python packaging. Note that these support the deployment and distribution of Meridian and are not runtime components but might be referenced as “Package & Environment Management” if needed.

3. Define Relationships and Data Flows
   - Data flows from the ingestion layer (data module) to the analysis and modeling modules. Represent directional arrows that show:
     • Data Collection/Preprocessing → Model Core
     • Model Core output → Analysis & Visualization (report generation, templating)
   - Depict an iterative loop where analysis results might inform adjustments in model parameters (e.g., calibration or optimization feedback).
   - For the CI/CD pipeline, show arrows from source code (GitHub version control) to automated testing/build, and ultimately to deployment/distribution.

4. Architectural Patterns and Key Technologies
   - Highlight that the framework leverages a modular design pattern by separating core functionalities into distinct packages (data, analysis, model).
   - Note the use of templating (Jinja2) for report generation, and the integration with GPU acceleration for model sampling (indicate this with a note on “GPU Support”).
   - Technologies & frameworks: Python (with its packaging tools), Jinja2 (for HTML templating), and TensorFlow Probability (for the NUTS sampler). You can add these as annotations or icons next to respective components.

5. Diagram Tailoring Guidelines
   - For a full-stack or comprehensive analytics application like Meridian, your system design diagram should emphasize:
     • The clear separation between the data ingestion layer, the modeling core, and the analysis/visualization layer.
     • The integration with CI/CD pipelines via GitHub Actions.
     • How user interactions (via demo notebooks and potentially API calls) feed into the system.
   - Use clear labels for each component (“Data Module”, “Model Engine”, “Analysis & Visualization”, etc.) and directional arrows to illustrate data flow.
   - Employ color coding (e.g., blue for data, green for modeling logic, and orange for visualization) or distinct shapes (rectangles for modules, cylinders for storage, etc.) to differentiate the pieces.

6. Detailed Diagram Elements to Include
   - Each component should have a clear label.
   - Arrows should indicate the flow of data or dependencies (for example, from “Input Data” to “Model Specification”, and then to “MCMC Sampling” followed by “Result Visualization”).
   - Consider annotating important submodules (like “adstock_hill”, “posterior_sampler”, “formatter” in the analysis module).
   - Optionally, include external system icons for GitHub Actions, GPU hardware, and user interfaces (demo notebooks).
   - Your drawing should capture the project’s modularity and how its individual parts interact to produce marketing mix modeling insights.

Following these guidelines will help you produce a diagram that accurately reflects the intricate but organized structure of Meridian, making it easier for stakeholders and engineers alike to understand the codebase and its operational flow.
</explanation>
